creatures.source: The snarling horned dragon lunging forward with unhinged jaws at the composition's apex

shape.summary: A chunky, toy-like draconic head and neck snapping forward with a cavernous black gullet, white fangs, and jutting horned crest.

creatures.pose: Head snapped forward in a gaping three-quarter roar, jaws parted to reveal sharp ivory fangs while the ear horn juts upward.
creatures.why: Translates the intense, coal-burnished dragon cranium into an imposing yet chunky low-poly guardian.

legend.R: raised ground (plateau, one or more blocks above G)

focal.what: the gaping jaws and unpupiled white eye of the wyvern head

composition.mass: Visual weight concentrates heavily in the upper-left and center-left where the tiered dragon head and spine rise above the floor.
composition.read: The eye enters along the lower-left looping path representing the gestural pencil tail, sweeps upward along the fractured slate ledges of the chest, and culminates at the raised roaring dragon cranium before tapering along the dorsal shards to the upper right.

lighting.notes: studio drawing lamp reflection on graphite: Directly quotes the extreme contrast between burnished lead sheen and blank white paper reserves.

rules: Place hatch shards along edges of raised plateau cliffs to mimic broken graphite crosshatching.
Keep the lower-left trail clear of obstructions to preserve the looping tail wireframe gesture.
Cluster spine frills immediately below the central wyvern head to emphasize the throat beard.

lens.place: a jagged quarry of carved anthracite and compressed lead shards rising out of blank parchment flats
lens.summary: Translates the contrast between dense burnished graphite hatching and open preliminary gesture loops into a fractured island of angular stone and vellum sand.
lens.differs: Replaces soft organic turf with razor-cut graphite slabs, crosshatch stone ridges, and looping wire trails.

shaper.name: shards
shaper.why: The drawing's dense multi-directional hatching and sharp needle-point contours map directly to fractured, overlapping angular slabs.

surface_mix.why: Sand represents the broad untouched toothy drawing paper, dirt carries the smudged mid-tone graphite haze, and stone highlights the sharpest burnished lead strokes while staying well within the twenty percent stone budget.

cliff_treatment.why: Sheer vertical cliff walls recall the razor-sharp pencil contours and deep dark pencil gouges carved into the drawing paper.

lighting.time: studio drawing lamp reflection on graphite
lighting.why: Directly quotes the extreme contrast between burnished lead sheen and blank white paper reserves.

concept.name: lens-medium
concept.fragment: LENS "medium": the artwork's MATERIAL AND MARKS become the island's physical character. Start from ANALYSIS.medium and ANALYSIS.palette, not from the subject. The ground is made of the marks: single-stroke ink becomes ribbon land and sweeping arcs of path with void where the paper is empty (shaper "ribbon", or "spiral" for a curl); airbrush gradients become soft radial terraces fading outward (shaper "radial"); fauvist or knife strokes become a patchwork of flat colour blocks at different heights (shaper "patchwork"); charcoal smudge becomes soft-edged dark masses with pale mist lying in the hollows (shaper "mound" or "basin"); pencil hatching or scratchy ink becomes angular slabs split by thin seams (shaper "shards"); vector doodles become dense small ornament on a tidy mirrored plan (shaper "symmetric"). Choose shaper params from the marks themselves (how many strokes, how wide, which way they sweep, how many blocks). Palette, surface_mix and cliff_treatment follow the medium (ink: paper-pale sand and ink-dark cliffs; airbrush: rings of surfaces fading by value; fauvist: saturated patches; charcoal: soft grey-green, mossy or soft cliffs). New props are the marks made solid: a brush flick as a curved blade of stone, a smudge as a low soft boulder, a doodle as a ring of beads, a knife stroke as a flat tilted slab. The figure's pose comes from how it is drawn (a single continuous stroke, a stack of colour patches), and it may be a monument of the marks rather than a living creature.
